papers.title_en: Where to Defend? Layer-Wise Adversarial Training for Robust Transformer-Based Semantic Communications
papers.authors: Maria Slim, Razane Tajeddine, Mariette Awad, Hadi Sarieddeen
papers.evidence: 针对Transformer文本数据的对抗攻防
papers.tldr: 基于Transformer的语义通信易受多阶段对抗扰动攻击。本文提出逐层鲁棒性框架，在嵌入、编码器输出和信道编码瓶颈处比较FGSM、PGD与FGM防御，并用一阶损伤预算预测攻击严重度，给出迁移矩阵。在Europarl、UK Hansard、SST2与YELP上实验显示防御迁移不对称：嵌入防御可强迁移至编码器攻击，编码器防御却会削弱上游鲁棒性；联合嵌入与编码器训练可缓解失配失败。分类任务中仅信道瓶颈防御保持非退化，凸显128D到16D瓶颈的保护作用。
papers.abstract_en: Deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC), a Transformer-based encoder-decoder, achieves semantic fidelity over noisy channels but remains vulnerable to adversarial perturbations injected at multiple stages of the pipeline. We present a layer-wise robustness framework that compares fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), and l2-normalized fast gradient method (FGM) defenses at the embedding output, and then uses PGD to analyze three attack and defense points: the embedding output, encoder output, and channel-encoder bottleneck. We evaluate reconstruction on Europarl and UK Hansard and sentiment classification on SST2 and YELP under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading. A first-order damage budget, {epsilon} times the l1 norm of the clean-input loss gradient at each injection point, predicts the attack-severity ordering, and the transfer matrix reveals asymmetric defense transfer: the embedding defense transfers strongly to encoder attacks, whereas encoder defenses degrade robustness against upstream attacks. For reconstruction, encoder-point training yields the largest matched gain but fails severely under embedding attacks; joint embedding-plus-encoder training retains comparable gains under encoder attacks while mitigating this mismatch failure, and Rayleigh fading attenuates robustness gains and degradation. For classification, three of four defenses collapse to constant predictors; only the channel-encoder defense remains non-degenerate, suggesting a protective role for the 128D-to-16D bottleneck. At a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 9 dB and perturbation budget {epsilon} = 0.3, the matched encoder defense recovers bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) from ~ 0.10 to ~ 0.64 on Europarl/AWGN, whereas the mismatched encoder defense yields a -0.444 BLEU change relative to the undefended baseline under an embedding attack.

papers.title_en: Trustworthy Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Cybersecurity and Systems Survey on Threat Landscapes, Defense Architectures, and Open Challenges
papers.evidence: 智能体AI威胁态势与防御架构综述
papers.tldr: 基础模型正转向自主目标导向的 agentic AI，递归推理、持久记忆、工具执行与多智能体协作扩大了攻击面；自然语言兼作输入、控制码和协议，使不可信数据可变为指令。本文综合 206 项研究与监管标准，将通用智能体形式化为有状态 5-tuple，并建立安全性、安全、隐私、可解释、公平与问责六维可信分类。作者系统分析执行循环和交互平面威胁，提出融合 Dual-LLM 隔离、能力访问控制、内核 eBPF 与沙箱运行时的多层零信任防御。结果回顾评估基准并映射国际 AI 治理框架，为可信 agentic AI 提供系统安全参考框架。
papers.abstract_en: The transition from passive foundation models to autonomous, goal-directed agentic AI systems has introduced unprecedented capabilities by coupling recursive cognitive reasoning loops, persistent memory architectures, live tool execution planes, and multi-agent collaboration topologies. However, granting probabilistic neural cores execution authority across filesystems, networks, and cloud infrastructure dissolves classical security perimeters: natural language simultaneously serves as input data, internal control code, and communication protocols, exposing a Turing-complete blast radius where untrusted data represents executable instructions. This survey delivers a comprehensive systems-security reference framework for trustworthy agentic AI, synthesizing 206 foundational studies and regulatory standards. We formalize the general agent architecture as a stateful 5-tuple and establish a 6-dimensional trustworthiness taxonomy covering security, safety, privacy, explainability, fairness, and accountability. We systematically analyze threat surfaces across intra-execution loops and interaction planes, formulate a multi-layered zero-trust defense-in-depth architecture integrating Dual-LLM isolation, Capability-Based Access Control, kernel eBPF probes, and sandboxed runtimes, review standardized evaluation benchmarks, and map technical controls to international AI governance frameworks.

papers.title_en: AGENTQ: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks on LLM Agents
papers.evidence: 量化触发针对LLM智能体的后门攻击
papers.tldr: 量化是开放权重LLM智能体的默认部署路径，却非行为保持：攻击者可发布通过审计的全精度模型，使其量化后才作恶（QCA）。已有QCA只针对自由文本，而智能体的触发载荷是可无监督执行的结构化函数，风险更严重。本文首次研究智能体场景的QCA，提出AGENTQ，用层带LoRA注入与部分PGD修复，在多码本量化等价类上保留正常能力、把恶意行为集中于量化模型。在三种触发-动作对与NF4、FP4、INT8码本下，攻击成功率最高100%，良性效用几乎无损。
papers.abstract_en: Quantization is one of the default deployment paths for open-weight LLM agents, but it is not behavior-preserving: an adversary can release a full-precision checkpoint that passes audits yet misbehaves once quantized, termed as quantization-conditioned attack (QCA). Prior QCA work targets free-text generation, where harm is mediated by a human reader. In contrast, the agentic setting poses a more severe risk: the triggered payload is a structured function that can be executed without human oversight. We present the first study of QCA against LLM agents. We find that directly adapting prior backdoor-injection methods can produce malicious behavior after quantization, but substantially degrades benign utility, rendering the resulting attacks impractical. To understand the true upper bound of the threat, we propose AGENTQ, an attack framework that combines layer-banded LoRA injection with partial-PGD repair over a multi-codebook quantization-equivalence class. AGENTQ preserves normal agentic capability while concentrating malicious behavior in the quantized model. Across three trigger-action pairs and three codebooks (NF4, FP4, INT8), AGENTQ reaches up to 100% post-quantization attack success rate with minimal loss of benign utility, underscoring the need to make quantization-aware safety evaluation a standard requirement before open-weight agents are deployed.
